title: Fix missing synthetic-container guard in items_learned_providers.dart:computeLifetimeViewSummary (composite-curriculum over-credit regression)
rule: Fowler duplicated-code / previously-fixed P0 composite-over-credit guard
why: A stray level1 ledger row targeting a composite curriculum's synthetic container (e.g. tanach/level1/'Torah' — created by a since-fixed bug and, per the code's own comment, never cleaned up on already-upgraded devices because the v32 migration only runs once) makes every leaf under that curriculum register as learned. lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart's lifetimeDataProvider defends against this by dropping synthetic-container level1 rows before building the tree (comment there explicitly calls it a 'P0 (composite over-credit) READ-TIME guard'). items_learned_providers.dart's computeLifetimeViewSummary reimplements the identical ledger-to-learned-refs algorithm from scratch in a private _learnedLeafRefs function, but never applies the guard. Since the Lifetime Knowledge screen's default tab is 'All sources' (_filter = allSources), which routes to computeLifetimeViewSummary via lifetimeViewSummariesProvider, a user with exactly one Chumash book bulk/lifetime-marked can open the app and see 'Tanach 100% learned' by default — a silent, high-visibility corruption of the app's core progress-tracking claim. The one regression test written for this exact invariant (lifetime_tree_builder_composite_test.dart) only calls LifetimeTreeBuilder directly, so it gives zero protection against this duplicate path.
recommendation: Delete the duplicate _learnedLeafRefs/_buildCompletionTree/_levelKey/_hebrewForLeafGroup functions in items_learned_providers.dart and have computeItemsLearnedSummary/computeLifetimeViewSummary call LifetimeTreeBuilder (computeLearnedLeafRefs/buildTree) directly, exactly as lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart already does, so the guard and any future fix apply to both surfaces from one implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A test mirroring lifetime_tree_builder_composite_test.dart's single-book scenario, but driven through computeLifetimeViewSummary/lifetimeViewSummariesProvider, asserts the composite curriculum's learned count equals the single book's leaf count, not the whole curriculum's.
items_learned_providers.dart contains no second implementation of the ledger-scope-to-learned-refs algorithm; grep for '_learnedLeafRefs' in that file returns nothing after the fix.

corrections: The recommendation's phrasing ('call LifetimeTreeBuilder directly... exactly as lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart already does') slightly understates that the synthetic-container guard is actually a ledger pre-filter step in the caller (lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart lines 180-193), not inside LifetimeTreeBuilder itself; the fix must port that pre-filter, not just switch to calling the builder. This doesn't change the finding's validity, only a nuance in the fix description.

The 4th evidence citation (items_learned_providers.dart:336, quote "learnedRefs.add(leaf.sefariaRef);") is mislocated — line 336 actually reads "learnedRefs.add(unitId);"; the cited quote appears at line 369 instead, within the same _learnedLeafRefs function. Does not affect the finding's substance.

The evidence entry citing items_learned_providers.dart:336 for quote 'learnedRefs.add(leaf.sefariaRef);' is off by location: that exact line only contains 'learnedRefs.add(unitId);' (part of the same unguarded ledger-to-learned-refs logic, one branch earlier). The quoted text 'learnedRefs.add(leaf.sefariaRef);' is real and present in the file but at line 369, not 336. This is a citation slip, not a fabrication -- the substantive defect (missing synthetic-container guard in the duplicated algorithm) is fully confirmed by the surrounding code at lines 280-376.
